title: node-3 suddenly shows NotReady
intro: Monitoring paged: node-3 flipped to NotReady ten minutes ago. Every pod that was running on it is now Unknown or stuck Terminating.

steps.prompt: Confirm the node's status and see if there's a stated reason.
steps.fake_output:
Conditions:
  Type             Status   Reason
  Ready            Unknown  NodeStatusUnknown
  MemoryPressure   Unknown  NodeStatusUnknown
Events:
  Warning  NodeNotReady  node-controller  Node node-3 status is now: NodeNotReady
steps.hint: describe node's Conditions section usually states why, or at least confirms the control plane has lost contact.

steps.prompt: Everything shows Unknown, meaning the control plane hasn't heard from this node's kubelet recently — not a resource pressure issue. Check events specifically for node-3 for any other clues.
steps.fake_output:
LAST SEEN   TYPE      REASON          MESSAGE
12m         Normal    NodeReady       Node node-3 status is now: NodeReady
2m          Warning   NodeNotReady    Node node-3 status is now: NodeNotReady
steps.hint: Filter events specifically to this node's name to cut out noise from everything else in the cluster.

steps.prompt: No clear cause in events — this points at kubelet on node-3 itself having stopped heartbeating, not something the API server can see. Check what pods were running there and their current state.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                    READY   STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE
billing-service-x7y8z   1/1     Unknown     0          3h
email-sender-a1b2c      1/1     Terminating 0          3h
steps.hint: Filtering pods by nodeName shows you exactly what's stranded on the unreachable node.

steps.prompt: These pods are stuck because the control plane can't confirm they're actually dead. Your infra team confirms node-3 is physically powered off for hardware replacement — force-delete the stuck pod so it can be rescheduled elsewhere.
steps.fake_output:
warning: Immediate deletion does not wait for confirmation that the running resource has been terminated. The resource may continue to run on the cluster indefinitely.
pod "billing-service-x7y8z" force deleted
steps.hint: Normal delete waits for kubelet to confirm termination — but kubelet on this node isn't responding, so a force delete is the only way to let the Deployment reschedule this pod elsewhere.

resolution: node-3's kubelet stopped heartbeating to the control plane — in this case because the underlying host was powered off for hardware replacement without draining it first. Because the control plane never received a clean shutdown signal, it couldn't confirm the node's pods had actually stopped, leaving them stuck in Unknown/Terminating instead of being cleanly rescheduled. The force-delete was safe here only because the node's total failure was independently confirmed (it was physically off) — force-deleting pods on a node that might still be running is genuinely risky, since it can lead to the same pod (or its storage) running in two places at once. The process gap: node-3 should have been cordoned and drained BEFORE the hardware work started, which would have rescheduled everything cleanly with zero pages.
